**Visualizing the Projection**

I'm now picturing a colored point within a colored boundary. My focus is on this point "casting" a cross – horizontal and vertical lines – extending outwards in all cardinal directions. These lines are the same color as the point and stop precisely when they encounter the boundary. This creates a visually distinct representation.

**Mapping the Grid's Structure**

I've established an interior point at (7, 4) with a value of 3, and the boundary is fixed at 9. I've successfully propagated the interior value along the top and bottom edges (columns 4, rows 2-6 and 8-13), changing their value to 3. I'm also now propagating along the left and right edges (columns 2, 3 row 7).

**Exploring Ray Propagation**

I've been tracing the propagation of values from a point (5,4) with a value of 5, using ray casting. The left and right rays are easily filled until they hit a boundary. I then determined the values that will propagate. I also investigated up and down propagation, I found a few mistakes and corrected them, confirming that values propagate correctly until hitting the boundary conditions. I also verified the 0 at row 9, col 4.
